title: Taiwan plans $4 bln Texas park to support Nvidia's AI supply chain - Bloomberg
source_used: Investing.com (via Yahoo Finance), citing Bloomberg; BigGo Finance, citing Bloomberg
key_facts: Taiwan plans several industrial parks in the US, each needing up to $4 billion; the first will be in Texas (Bloomberg, 16 Oct, citing Economy Minister Kung Ming-hsin).
Kung spoke to Bloomberg in an interview on 12 October; BigGo adds each park would cost $2 billion to $4 billion and that there will be 'more than one'.
The parks aim to help smaller Taiwanese suppliers set up in the US, supporting TSMC and Foxconn, Nvidia's key manufacturing partners.
The Taiwan Electrical and Electronic Manufacturers' Association will raise the funding; the government offers loan guarantees and help with US rules (BigGo adds visas and land).

Context: Taiwan faces pressure to meet investment commitments under its trade deal with Washington (BigGo: a $250 billion credit guarantee commitment) and to cut risk from tensions with China; TSMC has pledged $265 billion for US expansion.
quote_evidence: "We will build a long-term, sustainable supply chain locally — not just for Taiwanese companies, but American companies and local workers can participate as well," Kung said. (BigGo)
why_it_matters_hint: Taiwan's government is helping its chip supply chain move to the US alongside Nvidia's main makers.
notes: Bloomberg page not readable; read Investing.com's and BigGo's accounts of the same Bloomberg report. Site in Texas not named.
